title: Tier B — statistical oracle (backtest), strongest-partial only

ontology.definition: annualized mean excess return divided by its standard deviation
a date range never touched during signal construction

objective.claim: Signal S yields out-of-sample Sharpe > 1 on the pre-registered held-out period.

success.successCriterion: A strategy whose held-out backtest reports Sharpe > 1, with an argued reason the result is not an artifact of overfitting.
nonGoals: In-sample Sharpe > 1 — curve fitting, not evidence of generalization.
A single lucky held-out window presented as robust across regimes.

adversarialChecklist.check: confirm no future data enters signal computation at any timestamp
require a single pre-registered holdout evaluation, no re-runs

verifier.ceiling: A passing held-out backtest is evidence, not proof: it cannot rule out overfitting to that single window, a regime change after the sample, or transaction-cost and liquidity effects the model omits.
verifier.revisitIf: a longer out-of-sample period becomes available, or the strategy is deployed and produces live returns to compare against.

stopping.giveUpCondition: return the best surviving strategy after 2 consecutive empty rounds

forbiddenLookups: whether this exact signal is already published
